title: AC1024 physical associative dimension-dependency output and readback

profile.dependencyFields: class/status, read/write/attached/delegating flags, order, absent/empty name, dependency body ID/handle, and null read/node/write references
profile.bodyFields: AcDbAssocDimDependencyBody base/type records, version fields, and unique body name
profile.roles: dependency owned by the ACDBASSOC2DCONSTRAINTGROUP; dependency owns its body; dependency points to one DIMENSION entity that has exactly one matching reactor backlink; group action list contains the dependency once

implementation.summary: Added strict typed DXF parsing for the emitted ASSOCDIMDEPENDENCYBODY sequence, source snapshots and unchanged-source checks for all 17 physical dependency/body pairs, staged OBJECTS inspection and output finalization. Source entity handles are mapped through the entity handle remapper. The selector reimports ASCII and binary output and compares every dependency/body field, pair identity, dependency owner/body role, dimension target and reactor backlink. Constraint-group action membership is checked; complete constraint-node tail parsing is not claimed.
implementation.failureBehavior: A late body-name mutation after OBJECTS emission refuses publication and preserves a preexisting destination sentinel. Restoring the source name and retrying on the same adapter succeeds. Both ASCII and binary paths exercise these controls.
implementation.fixturePolicy: Reused the existing local mechanical DWG. No test DWG or DXF fixture was added to the repository; generated outputs are temporary.

limitations: The CLI proof uses explicit partial DWG-read mode. The physical source still reports 228 opaque callbacks and zero retained correlation frames, so strict complete-export admission remains closed.
The readback proves the dependency's group action membership but does not prove full constraint-group node-tail semantic parsing.
This profile proof does not close the other physical callback profiles or qualify LibreCAD, LibreCAD_3, FreeCAD, native platforms, packaging, ABI, 3D semantics, or any support claim.
